gap: No result ChatGPT got states what a NAS draws from the wall or what that power costs. Dong Knows measured the Synology DS225+ at about 275 Wh per 24 hours with two hard drives. At the August 2026 US residential average of 18.16¢/kWh, that is about $55 over three years. KitGuru measured the UGREEN DXP4800 Plus at 24.25 W idle, which works out to about $116.
standout_why: I compared against ChatGPT's cited pages: the Synology Drive tech spec, the Drive Admin Console KB and the Drive Quick Start KB. I also checked the top uncited results: the QuickConnect KB and white paper, the DSM security KB and the DSM spec pages. None of them has a measured power figure or a measured remote (QuickConnect relay) throughput figure. The Drive spec says only that concurrent client connections 'vary by model'. ChatGPT's cost table lists 'Backup, electricity, maintenance' as 'Additional' with no number. Our current cost3y column also leaves electricity out.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. Measured electricity adds roughly $55 (DS225+) to $116 (DXP4800 Plus idle) over three years. Even with that added, a 2-bay NAS plus drives and B2 costs well under Google Workspace Business Standard at $2,520 for 5 seats over 3 years. It also favours a 2-bay over the 4-bay DXP4800 Plus for 5 people, by about $60 in electricity over 3 years. Electricity is not the deciding factor; upload bandwidth and the admin work are.

findings.label: Measured energy use per 24 hours
findings.value: ≈275 Wh per 24 h (tested with two hard drives)
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ Review (vs. DS224+): A Solid Upgrade to 2.5GbE Connectivity — Dong Ngo, Dong Knows Tech, 2025-08-04
findings.note: Dong Ngo's spec table; the review does not name the drives used for this test. Average draw is about 11.5 W (my arithmetic: 275/24). Per year: 275 Wh × 365 = 100.4 kWh. Over 3 years: 301 kWh × $0.1816 = about $55.

findings.label: Measured idle power at the wall
findings.value: 24.25 W idle (2.5GbE); 30.45 W idle (10GbE); peak 52.07 W read and 61.35 W write (2.5GbE)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800Plus 4-bay NAS Review — Simon Crisp, KitGuru, 2024-05-28
findings.note: Measured at the wall during CrystalDiskMark 8.0.4 with WD Red WD60EFRX drives; the number of drives is not stated. Assuming it idles all day at 2.5GbE: 24.25 W × 8,760 h = 212 kWh a year, or 637 kWh over 3 years × $0.1816 = about $116.

findings.label: Measured idle and maximum power
findings.value: ≈7 W idle; 34.7 W maximum (CPU, RAM and disk stress test)
findings.source_title: Ugreen DXP2800 NAS Review — Practical testing, OCinside.de (undated, author not shown)
findings.note: The review does not say which drives were installed for the idle figure, so it likely understates idle draw with two spinning HDDs. 7 W × 8,760 h = 61 kWh a year; over 3 years 184 kWh × $0.1816 = about $33 (lower bound).

findings.label: Measured standby and data-transfer power at the wall (SSD only)
findings.value: 5.6 W standby; 14.5 W during data transfer; 0.6 W off with WoL
findings.source_title: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 NAS im Test — Tim Kutzner, igor'sLAB, 2024-05-08 (modified 2025-05-31)
findings.note: Measured at the wall socket with one NVMe SSD and no hard drives, so add the drives' own draw for a real setup.

findings.product: UGREEN NASync DXP2800 GT (sibling of the DXP2800, for HDD-loaded reference)
findings.label: Measured idle power with two HDDs spinning
findings.value: 14.84–20.14 W idle; 35.9 W maximum (CPU + drives); 29.11 dB(A) idle at 30 cm
findings.source_title: Small, fast and surprisingly quiet: Ugreen NASync DXP2800 GT review — Daniel Schmidt, Notebookcheck, 2026-10-13
findings.note: Two WD Red drives installed and spinning. This is the GT model, not our N100 DXP2800; it is the only named lab figure for a 2-bay UGREEN with HDDs spinning. Over 3 years: 390–529 kWh × $0.1816 = about $71–96.

findings.label: Measured SMB transfer over 2.5GbE (LAN)
findings.value: 282 MB/s read, 263 MB/s write (34.51 GB file to/from a Mac Studio)
findings.source_title: Synology DS225+ review — Luka Manestar, BLACKVOID.CLUB, 2025-09-08
findings.note: These are LAN figures. For remote users the NAS site's upload speed caps throughput long before this, so this shows the box is not the bottleneck.

findings.label: Measured throughput over 2.5GbE (LAN, IOMeter-style traces)
findings.source_title: Ugreen NASync DXP4800Plus 4-bay NAS Review — Simon Crisp, KitGuru, 2024-05-28
findings.note: Averages over 2.5GbE. This is a LAN figure and not relevant to remote limits.

findings.label: Synology's own power figures and Drive user rating (maker spec, not a reviewer measurement)
findings.value: 16.98 W access; 6.08 W HDD hibernation; Synology Drive maximum 10 users
findings.note: Synology bases the 10-user figure on 20% of users doing file operations and 80% logged in but idle; going over it 'may result in longer response time'. NASCompares' DS225+ review (2025-08-04) repeats 16.98 W / 6.08 W, so I did not count that as an independent measurement.

findings.label: US average residential electricity price (used for the cost arithmetic)
findings.note: I used this in every 3-year electricity calculation above. The NAS would run in an office or home, so I used the residential rate (the all-sector rate is 14.87¢).

unsourced: Measured remote throughput through Synology QuickConnect relay vs a direct/DDNS connection. I looked at WunderTech's remote-access comparison, SynoForum threads and Synology KB; I found only forum anecdotes (about 0.5 MB/s, about 2 Mb/s) with no named reviewer or lab.
Measured UGREENlink relay speed. igor'sLAB's DXP2800 remote-access page (page 7) describes the relay but gives no speed; the KitGuru and TechPowerUp (403) DXP4800 Plus reviews have no remote speed.
A named reviewer's idle wattage for the N100 DXP2800 with two HDDs spinning. OCinside does not state its drives, igor'sLAB used an SSD only, and Notebookcheck tested the GT variant.
Any named measurement of Synology Drive sync latency or Synology Office co-editing performance with several users. Blackvoid, Dong Knows and NASCompares ran no Drive or Office tests.
igor'sLAB DXP4800 Plus power page (returned 403), so I could not confirm its standby figure.
